The tree already reads as [the node path](#the-node-path) does, a node passed last: `type`, `start`, `end`, `range`, `name`, `value`, `field`, `fieldCount`, `flag` and `textOf` with the `NodeType`, `Field`, `Flag` and `Part` that `syntax.parser` exports. `SourceProcessor` walks the tree a parse writes as the CSS and HTML ones walk theirs, each visitor handed that path and the children taken in source order (a template's quasis and expressions in turn). Asked for `mode: "minify"`, the same walk prints: `syntax-printer.js`'s `printer` returns each node's text from its children's, as `minify` prints a source it neither compresses nor mangles, comments left out and terser's format options read from `format`. `minify` prints such a source with it too where no source map is asked for and not every comment is kept (which `printTree` prints with fewer instructions), walking the tree its own parse wrote (`walkSyntaxTree`) with the comments it keeps, a name printed inside its parent's text where none of its own is read: each is taken as terser's printer reaches it, by the node holding its token, and printed once the text before it is, which a text opening with it leaves to the node printing that text. - `syntax-parser.js` — tokenizer, acorn-derived core and every production in one file (any parse reaches the productions). Given a `syntaxTree`, the lazy path writes each node into it as it finishes, an id in the tree's columns rather than an object; the few the parser reads back by name (a key, a module name, an exported declaration, a function before its body ends) stay objects until their parent is written, and an expression read as a pattern after all is retyped in place. Only the latest edition without parser plugins takes a tree, since acorn's own productions read their nodes back. `regexp.js` (pattern validator) is the one on-demand piece, reached only for a pattern the host engine rejected — never `require` it from a build path.

- Printing and mangling read the compressed tree as it is held, by its ESTree types: no conversion step stands between the compressor and the printer, so a tree a caller passes in or `format.ast` hands back is printed and mangled as it is. Where the compressor holds a shape of its own the printer reads it directly — a template's `segments`, two side by side printing as one text; an import's `imported_name` and `imported_names`, an export's `exported_definition`, `exported_value` and `exported_names`, attributes as the object holding them; `import()`'s `args`; a key's or a property read's name as a symbol node; a literal's `role` for a regular expression or a bigint's digits — and a name prints as its `definition` names it (`mangled_name`, else the definition's own name), terser's or the mangler's alike, never renamed in place. Where nobody keeps the tree, `analyzeManglingScopes` and `printProgram` drop what only the compressor read (`COMPRESSOR_ONLY_FIELDS`) off each node they read; every field written is one its kind's factory made. The `estreeMangle` phase mangles that tree as terser's mangler did: `analyzeManglingScopes` resolves its scopes, writing each name's `definition`, `computeEstreeCharFrequency` orders the identifiers, `mangleManglingScopes` gives the definitions their `mangled_name` and `renameMangledEstree` renames `#private` names and properties in one walk, skipped where there are neither. `printEstree` (the `estreePrint` phase) dispatches on `node.type` through three tables — `codegen` (the text), `needsParens` and `sourceMapping` — and asks about a parent through the `kindOf` predicates, never `instanceof`; the stream (`MinifiedOutput`) reads comments through `NodeAccess`. Everything that prints goes through it: `minify`, the mangler's character frequency and the compressor's `printToString`.
